Attached: 4 images

After completing work in Village 5, we have to negotiate another four-hour walk under wind and rain to reach Village 6. Bougainville has been hit by a tropical storm, the first of this kind in this equatorial area, so the conditions of the paths we walk on are particularly treacherous. Despite this, Pouka resident John lifts the massive weight of my power generator system onto his back and carries it along the path. I have no idea how he manages, but these people do more or less the same every week when they carry bags of potatoes, bananas, or other crops to be sold on the market. He has no protection on his back, and he uses ropes made from dried sago leaves. Other local residents escort me and carry all of my other research materials. 

Videos on my YT channel: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLflfu1fp428M
